quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.hint: Break the word into parts -- does it sound like a small number, a "teen", or a bigger one?
quests.explanation: "Three Hundred Sixty-Nine" is how we say the number 369 in English, so 369 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: Double 369 is 738! Because 369 + 369 = 738.

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 307, 427, or 462?
quests.hint: Compare them two at a time, then keep the bigger one.
quests.explanation: Out of 307, 427, and 462, the number 462 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 462, you get 463!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 384 or 273?
quests.hint: Compare the digits from left to right: which number has more value?
quests.explanation: 384 is greater than 273 -- when counting up, 384 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you had 384 apples and found one more, you would have 385 apples!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 320, 369, or 386?
quests.hint: Compare them two at a time, then keep the bigger one.
quests.explanation: Out of 320, 369, and 386, the number 386 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 386 by 10, it becomes 3860!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the tens place of 341?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the tens digit in 341.
quests.explanation: In 341, the digit 4 sits in the tens place!
quests.funFact: The number 4 is a single-digit number, meaning it only takes up one spot!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Count up to 261 in your head, saying each number word as you go.
quests.explanation: The numeral 261 is written in words as "Two Hundred Sixty-One" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: When you can read big math words like 'Two Hundred Sixty-One', you are becoming a true math master!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 25, 75, 125, 175, __?
quests.hint: Add the same jump size again to the last number in the pattern.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 50, so after 175 comes 175 + 50 = 225!
quests.funFact: The number 225 is an odd number!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the tens place of 500?
quests.hint: Split 500 into its place-value parts, then find the tens part.
quests.explanation: In 500, the digit 0 sits in the tens place!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to any number, that number stays exactly the same!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Look at how many digits 406 has, then think of how that word usually sounds.
quests.explanation: The numeral 406 is written in words as "Four Hundred Six" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: The word 'Four Hundred Six' helps us communicate numbers without just drawing shapes!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the hundreds place of 416?
quests.hint: Count from the right: ones first, then tens, then hundreds -- find the hundreds spot.
quests.explanation: In 416, the digit 4 sits in the hundreds place!
quests.funFact: Double 4 is 8! Because 4 + 4 = 8.

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 155, 476, or 219?
quests.hint: Line all three numbers up in counting order first.
quests.explanation: Out of 155, 476, and 219, the number 476 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: Double 476 is 952! Because 476 + 476 = 952.

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 492 or 453?

quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 492, you get 493!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the hundreds place of 189?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the hundreds digit in 189.
quests.explanation: In 189, the digit 1 sits in the hundreds place!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 1 by 10, it becomes 10!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 186 or 234?
quests.hint: Picture counting all the way up -- whichever number you'd reach later is the answer.
quests.explanation: 234 is greater than 186 -- when counting up, 234 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 234 by 10, it becomes 2340!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!

quests.explanation: The numeral 328 is written in words as "Three Hundred Twenty-Eight" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: Did you know? The math word 'Three Hundred Twenty-Eight' is spelled with exactly 23 letters!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 0, 50, 100, 150, __?
quests.hint: The pattern counts up by 50 each time. What comes after 150?
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 50, so after 150 comes 150 + 50 = 200!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to 200, it stays exactly the same: 200!

quests.explanation: Out of 440, 322, and 157, the number 157 is the smallest!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 157 comes right after 156!

quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 10, so after 30 comes 30 + 10 = 40!
